answer: Hash-chained work ledger stops Sybils in four steps. First, each real job receipt is hashed and chained to the previous one, so history cannot be rewritten or backdated. Second, seven rotating agents notarize each chain every week; one broken link freezes the account. Third, newcomers post a $40 bond; tampering burns it and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, job limits grow as the verified chain lengthens. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 chains and $40,000 in bonds, all lost when caught. Like a cedar bridge over shale, one rotten plank betrays the whole span.
